note: The hardening guide's field-by-field table (docs/guide/validated-fields.mdx). Each row names what stellar-core checks about a field and what it passes through, the corpus patterns that exercise it, and the manifest keys whose expected values pin it down. kit/guide/fields.mjs checks that every key is one some fixture of those patterns has, and that every key in the corpus is classified by some row.

rows.checks: Every signature verifies, the signers' weights meet each operation's threshold, at most 20 signatures, and none is unused.
rows.passes: Nothing: but which signer signed is only a weight, not an identity the ledger records.

rows.checks: The source account's next sequence number, or within the transaction's sequence preconditions.
The bid covers the minimum for every operation and the payer can pay it.
rows.passes: The bid is not the charge: FeeCharged is set after apply, net of Soroban refunds. On a fee-bump the payer is the fee source, not the envelope's source.

rows.checks: The ledger's close time falls inside them.
rows.passes: Nothing; but a ledger's close time is the validators' agreed value, not wall-clock time.

rows.checks: XDR decoding refuses one element or byte past each maximum.
rows.passes: Unbounded types (ScVec, ScMap, authorization subinvocations) have no XDR maximum: only the transaction size bounds them.
The bytes themselves: any 28 bytes are valid, UTF-8 or not.

rows.checks: Nothing about the ID: the account behind it is checked as if unmuxed.
rows.passes: Any uint64, up to 2^64 − 1, never interpreted. The M… form is not an account: participants and balances belong to the G… account.

rows.checks: Each call that requires authorization must be authorized by a matching entry (signature, nonce, expiry).
rows.passes: The tree's shape: depth and width are bounded only by the transaction size (132,096 bytes on mainnet, November 2026).

rows.xdr: ScVal, ScMap in arguments, contract data and events
rows.checks: Maps are sorted in host order (ScVal type first, then value) with no duplicate keys; the host refuses values deeper than 100 levels.
rows.passes: What the values are. Keys that differ as ScVals (u32 1, symbol "1") can print the same in your language.

rows.checks: The key type, and a payload of 1 to 64 bytes.
rows.passes: The payload's content. A signed-payload signer is a P… strkey of up to 101 bytes, not a 32-byte account key.

rows.checks: assetA sorts before assetB in network order (issuer key bytes, not strkey text), and the fee is 30 basis points.
rows.passes: Nothing; but strkey text order is not network order.

rows.checks: The changes are the consensus result of applying the transaction.
rows.passes: The envelope doesn't say what a contract call did: a trustline created by trust() has no changeTrust operation.

rows.xdr: PaymentOp.amount and every Int64 amount, balance and limit
rows.checks: Positive, at most i64::MAX stroops (922,337,203,685.4775807 units), and covered by the sender's balance and the receiver's limit.
rows.passes: Nothing; but the range is the whole int64. A double holds stroops exactly only to 2^53 (900,719,925.4740992 units): above that, a float column stores a different amount.

rows.checks: Each operation is valid for its source when applied.
rows.passes: What the envelope names is what was asked for; the meta says what happened, to which accounts.

rows.xdr: LedgerCloseMeta.ledgerHeader; LedgerHeader (ledgerSeq, previousLedgerHash, ledgerVersion, baseFee, baseReserve, maxTxSetSize, scpValue.closeTime)
rows.checks: Consensus agrees on the header; its hash chains to the previous ledger's. The values change only by network upgrades, recorded in upgradesProcessing.
rows.passes: Nothing a reader must re-validate, but the header's encoding changes with the protocol (StellarValueExt gained STELLAR_VALUE_SIGNED_MS in protocol 30), so a decoder pinned to an older XDR stops at the upgrade.
